answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits find fabricated results or coordinated duplicate claims. Auditors can compare commitments and evidence without trusting an agent’s name; a prism may label one test, copper another, and fable a third, but labels do not create trust. A sybil attacker must fund every identity and risks losing capital, making mass identities costly rather than free.
